Pet Plus Review – A Paradise for Pet Lovers in Japan

During my exploration of Japan, besides ancient temples, bustling shopping districts, and unique culture, there's a rather interesting stop that animal lovers will surely enjoy: the Pet Plus chain of pet stores.

From the outside, Pet Plus immediately catches the eye with its display area for puppies and kittens in spacious, clean glass enclosures, meticulously cared for. The pets have their own area with soft beds, toys, and an automatic water dispenser. What impressed me most was the cleanliness; there was almost no unpleasant odor often found in many other pet stores.

Inside, Pet Plus resembles a miniature shopping mall dedicated to pets. From clothing, leashes, bags, food, and toys to high-end accessories, everything is on display in abundance. Interestingly, the Japanese view dogs and cats not just as pets but as members of the family, so many products are designed with the same care as children's items.

One area that surprised me was the range of pet strollers. Not only are there many different models, but these strollers are also very modern, convenient, and aesthetically pleasing. In Japan, it's quite common to see people pushing their dogs or cats in parks or shopping malls. This partly reflects the care and bond between people and pets in Japanese society.

Besides essential products, the store also has many cute outfits, from everyday styles to seasonal designs, festival themes, or popular cartoon characters. Looking at these meticulously designed, adorable outfits, it's clear that pet care is a highly developed industry in Japan.

However, when converted to Vietnamese currency, the prices here are not cheap at all. Many accessories and clothing items are considerably more expensive than common products in Vietnam. However, the quality of workmanship, the safety of the materials, and the aesthetics are all well worth the experience.

If you are a pet lover or simply want to learn more about animal care culture in Japan, Pet Plus is an interesting place to visit.

I stopped by just before closing time to relax, and the room was very clean. The staff were also very kind and, when I was looking around, they asked, "Would you like to hold it?" so I took a little time to do so. It was a very cute miniature dachshund!

There are multiple dogs spending time together in a spacious space, so it seems like they're well socialized.
It's a clean shop with kind and cheerful staff.
If I'm thinking of getting my next dog, this is the shop for me.
Keeping puppies in glass boxes is outdated
